description:
FOUND s465ba (Opus, round 23) while attributing #1028's movers.  The bug is in
the instrument, not the product.  PRE-EXISTING.

tools/sweep-diff.pl:157-166 builds its record map as

    %rec;   # "file\tdesc" => { file, desc, got, expected, num }
    ...
    $rec{"$file\t$desc"} = { ... };

so two failing rows in the same file with an EMPTY description overwrite each
other.  perl-tests/bop.t's own header says "Tests don't have names yet", and it
currently produces FOURTEEN unnamed failing rows (test numbers 50 55 60 80 116
117 121 122 126 127 132 137 142 146, every one `got '2', expected '1'` -- the
tied-scalar `is(fetches($x), 1)` rows).  baselines/fail-baseline.tsv holds ONE
unnamed bop.t entry (test 144), and the gate reports 0 new.

MEASURED, so the collapse is not theoretical: a `--jobs 1` run of bop.t on
1fed80b and on the #1028 tree produce byte-identical unnamed-row sets (14 rows,
same numbers, same values), and the full-sweep gate says "0 new" on both -- but
it would say "0 new" just as happily if a change added a fifteenth.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND bop.t: this is the same family as s464ay's finding that
"fully passing" was not a fact about PCL.  A file whose rows have no
descriptions has, in effect, ONE gated row no matter how many it produces.
Count the population first: how many files produce more than one unnamed
failing row, and how many rows hide behind the collapse across the whole
sweep AND `tools/run-perl-suite.pl`.

FIX SHAPE (untried): key on "file\tdesc" when desc is non-empty and
"file\t#NUM" when it is not -- the key scratch/cmp-bop.pl (this session's
throwaway comparator) used to find the 14.  NOTE the standing rule that a test
NUMBER is only meaningful within its own run (DECIDED s386 ask 3), which is
exactly why unnamed rows are unsafe to gate by number in a file that ABORTS at
a different point run to run -- so the fix probably has to pair the number key
with the file's PARTIAL/OK status, or leave those rows UNVERIFIED rather than
silently matched.  Design before coding.

Also worth checking in the same pass: the blessed `bop.t 144` row does not
reproduce on 1fed80b either (the live run has no unnamed row 144), so at least
one baseline entry is stale in a way the collapse hides.
subject: MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT GAP: `tools/sweep-diff.pl` keys a failing row on "file\tdescription", so EVERY unnamed row in one file collapses to a single key -- perl-tests/bop.t's 14 unnamed failures are all one baseline entry, and 13 of them are invisible to the gate.  A regression that adds an unnamed failing row to a file that already has one cannot be seen.
